chunks: If you do not help (the Prophet, remember) God had helped him when the infidels had forced him to leave (and he was) one of two. When both of them were in the cave, he said to his companion: "Do not grieve, for God is with us." Then God sent divine peace on him, and invisible armies for his help, and made the unbelievers' purpose abject. Most exalted is God's word, for God is all-mighty and all-wise.

key_terms.إِلَّا تَنْصُرُوهُ: If you do not help him
key_terms.ثَانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ: One of two / the second of two

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the cave of Thawr and God's unseen help mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is pivotal for establishing the concept of divine assistance (nasr) and tranquility (sakinah) specifically bestowed upon the Prophet and his caliph, Abu Bakr, during the Hijrah. The mention of 'unseen troops' (junud lam tarawha) is interpreted as angels who aided in securing the cave, symbolizing God's power to elevate His word over the disbelievers' words. This event serves as a foundational precedent for the legitimacy of the Prophet's leadership and the divine protection of the Islamic community during its critical transition from Mecca to Medina.
